analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily (2026-10-26)
key_insights: USTs gave back part of Thursday's safe-haven rally, driven by stabilising European sovereign risk, firmer tech and higher oil. WTI rose 3.6% to $103.27, pushing 2y yields back to 4.70% and 10y yields to test 5.00%, with 2s10s about 0.5bp flatter.
US PMIs were solid (manufacturing 56.0, services 57.9) but secondary to the cross-asset move. They are consistent with resilient activity while oil keeps inflation concerns in focus.

Markets price a 13% chance of a Fed hike at Wednesday's FOMC and about 22.5bp of hikes by December. Peak OIS forwards rebounded toward 4.55%, so the meeting is about the Fed's signalling on the path ahead rather than an immediate move.

French political risk premium eased and OATs outperformed despite weak French PMIs. The 10y OAT-Bund spread tightened 5.5bp to 168.5bp, having traded around 170-173bp earlier, and BTPs also recovered versus Bunds.

Bund 10y yields fell to 3.31% before rising oil reversed the move, briefly reaching 3.36% and closing near 3.34%. Tighter peripheral spreads came with little outright duration follow-through as the energy impulse offset softer French growth.

Moody's is widely expected to downgrade France to A1. French manufacturing and services PMIs remain in contraction while German manufacturing is firmer. EUR/USD edged up about 0.1% to 1.1216, snapping four straight sessions of losses.

Gilts gave back Thursday's gains after a clear UK PMI beat (manufacturing 52.8, services 53.1) with elevated price pressures and new highs in UK natural gas, which weighed on the front end. The 10y yield rose 2.6bp to 5.351%, 2s30s flattened 1.5bp, and 10s30s flattened for a seventh straight session at about 38bp.

The 10y Gilt-Bund spread is back above 200bp. Focus shifts to Wednesday's UK Budget, with domestic fiscal and supply risk replacing externally driven risk-off support, including speculation that DMO allocation buckets could be restructured. GBP/USD is marginally softer around 1.3356.

JGBs twist flattened, with strength concentrated in the ultra-long end (15-20y demand strongest) ahead of the 5-11y tap auction. The 20y and 30y richened about 2.5bp and 3bp respectively, and 20s30s bull flattened, while the 2y and 5y upside stayed capped.
The yen fell 0.64% to 157.13 on broad dollar softness. USD/JPY is at 157.17, with the yen near a one-month high against the dollar. DXY is flat around 101.80.
